messages.content: Contemplate on few lines of “Part four” (page 153) of this novel, “Majid: Wake up, Bibi. I am going to take both of you to the village. When Majeed came out of the house carrying Jamila, wrapped in a thin... quilt, a bewilderedRahima at his heels, the brilliant moonlight at first blinded him.” Even if Majeed was mostly depicted as a cunning and apathetic person throughout the narrative, do you find the same character traits in the mentioned lines? Was he trying to save Rahima and Jamila out of good-will (deontology) or his action was well-calculated (teleology)?Explain it. Include at least 10 single-word palindromes, each at least 5 characters long.

message.content:
Yes, the same traits are visible, though compressed into a single decisive moment. Majeed’s words are functional, not comforting: “Wake up, Bibi. I am going to take both of you to the village.” There is no apology, no reassurance, no pause for Rahima’s bewilderment. He moves the people as if they were parts of a plan. Jamila is “wrapped in a thin... quilt,” which suggests haste and exposure rather than tenderness. Rahima follows “at his heels,” not beside him as an equal; she is being managed, not consulted. Even the moonlight blinding him reads less like moral awakening and more like a physical obstacle he is prepared to push through. The passage therefore reinforces his cunning and emotional distance: he acts, but he does not become gentle.

Ethically, the action appears more teleological than deontological. If Majeed were acting from good-will in a deontological sense, the rescue would be motivated by duty or the intrinsic rightness of saving them, with Rahima and Jamila treated as ends in themselves. Here, however, his action reads as well-calculated: the village is the more useful destination, the safer or more orderly outcome, the move that serves his next step. Saving them may reduce danger, preserve control, or protect his position. There is a protective gesture, but it is instrumental rather than disinterested compassion. Rahima and Jamila are not abandoned, but they are also not purely objects of moral concern; they are factors in his strategy. Thus the scene preserves his character: he saves them because it is expedient, not because warm goodwill overcomes his calculation.

Palindromes: radar, refer, civic, stats, rotor, rotator, racecar, redder, reviver, tenet.
